title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to Grothendieck's notes on the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}. The Deligne–Mumford compactification is stratified by stable dual graphs, which he calls MD-graphs (Mumford–Deligne). For each graph G:
- M_G is the open stratum and ΠM_G its fundamental groupoid.
- Γ = Aut G acts on these objects.
- A = A(G) is the set of edges, i.e. the double points.
- S_AΠM_G (or SΠM_G) is the fundamental groupoid of the 'punctured tubular neighbourhood' of M_G. It is an extension of ΠM_G by Z^A, generated by the Dehn twists around the vanishing cycles.

Topologically, S_AΠM_G is π1 of the (S^1)^A-torus bundle over M_G. This bundle is the corner stratum of the real oriented blow-up of the boundary divisor, equivalently the Kato–Nakayama log-Betti space or the Harvey bordification.

Previous page. For a contraction G → G' = G/C (C ⊂ A), dividing by the twists along A∖C gives the quotient extension S_CΠM_G of ΠM_G by Z^C. The morphism (119) S_AΠM_G → S_{A'}ΠM_{G'} is compatible with Γ_{G,G'}, the stabiliser of the contraction.

This page.
- (121): the map factors through (S_CΠM_G, Γ^!_{G,G'}) → ΠM_{G'}. Here Γ^!_{G,G'} is the subgroup acting trivially on G'. Geometrically: near M_G, smoothing only the nodes in C lands in the stratum M_{G'}. The punctured neighbourhood of M_G inside the closure of M_{G'} maps to M_{G'}, and on π1 this gives a map from the Z^C-extension.
- (122): more generally, for Γ^! ⊂ Γ' ⊂ Γ_{G,G'} (subgroups stabilising C), one gets (S_CΠM_G, Γ') → (ΠM_{G'}, Γ'/Γ^!). The target is identified with (ΠM_{G,G'}, Γ'/Γ^!), where M_{G,G'} is the 'link' piece of M_{G'} near M_G.
- He observes that the earlier transitivity relation (105) just says that G ↦ S_AΠM_G is a functor on the category of MD-graphs and generalisation morphisms (edge contractions).

Start of an axiomatisation. MD-graphs with generalisation morphisms form a category 𝒢 in which every morphism is an epimorphism. The next page adds two conditions:
- (Simpl): the poset of proper quotients of each G is the Boolean lattice of subsets of a finite set A_G (the edges).
- Each G carries an extension SΠM_G → ΠM_G by Z^{A_G}, functorial in G, with partial quotients by Z^C for C ⊂ A_G.

Purpose. This is an abstract, combinatorial–groupoid model of how the fundamental groupoids of the strata of the DM compactification glue along tubular neighbourhoods. It serves the Esquisse programme of describing the Teichmüller tower and its Galois action 'at infinity'.
errors: (122) is written with S_S where S_C is clearly meant; this is a slip.
The identification of the target of (122) with (ΠM_{G,G'}, Γ'/Γ^!) is stated without justification. It depends on the definition of M_{G,G'} given earlier, which is not on this page.
There is a minor grammatical/notational inconsistency: 'les groupoïdes S_AΠM_G dépend'. No mathematical error is visible.

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of the punctured tubular neighbourhood of a boundary stratum as an extension of ΠM_G by Z^{edges}, generated by Dehn twists; quotient extensions S_C for subsets C of edges.
ideas.modern_name: π1 of corner strata of the real oriented blow-up / Kato–Nakayama space / Harvey bordification; boundary (cusp) subgroups of the mapping class group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Harvey (bordification, 1970s); Ihara–Nakamura, Boggi (profinite setting); Kato–Nakayama (log Betti realisation, 1999)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the 'structure à l'infini' and tubular neighbourhoods, without these formulas

ideas.what: Factorisation (121)/(122): the Z^C-extension, with the residual automorphism group Γ'/Γ^!, maps to the fundamental groupoid of the more generic stratum M_{G/C}.
ideas.modern_name: Specialisation/cospecialisation maps between strata; exit-path data of a stratified space

ideas.what: Transitivity of the gluing data recast as functoriality of G ↦ S_AΠM_G on the category of stable graphs with contraction morphisms.
ideas.modern_name: Functor on the category of stable graphs (Getzler–Kapranov modular operads; Feynman categories)

ideas.what: Axiom (Simpl): a category where all morphisms are epimorphisms and each object's poset of quotients is the Boolean lattice of a finite set; used as the abstract indexing category for the gluing data.
ideas.modern_name: Boolean / cubical Reedy-type indexing category; the face poset of a toroidal (normal crossings) stratification
ideas.usually_credited_to: unclear; implicit in normal-crossings/toroidal geometry and graph complexes

missed.claim: Grothendieck begins an abstract axiomatisation of the 'structure at infinity'. The data are: a category of graphs with Boolean quotient posets, plus a functorial system of groupoids ΠM_G with Z^{A(G)}-extensions SΠM_G and partial quotients S_C mapping to ΠM_{G/C}. This amounts to a combinatorial model of the stratified/log fundamental groupoid of a normal-crossings compactification. It looks like a discrete precursor of exit-path or log-Betti descriptions. The axiomatisation appears to be left unfinished in these notes.
missed.quote: On va axiomatiser un peu. Les MD-graphes et morphismes de généralisation forment une catégorie, (𝒢), où tous les morphismes sont des épimorphismes. Cette catégorie satisfait
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with Boggi's profinite description of the boundary of the curve complex, and with Kato–Nakayama/log-Betti fundamental groupoids of the DM stack. It also bears on van Kampen-type reconstructions of the Teichmüller (Grothendieck–Teichmüller) tower from its strata. An explicit axiom system of this type, tied to Galois actions on M_{g,ν}, is not standard in the literature.

missed.claim: Grothendieck's indexing category of stable graphs with contractions is used as the base of a 'diagram of groupoids'. The same category later underlies Getzler–Kapranov modular operads. Here it is paired with fundamental-groupoid extensions rather than with (co)homology.
missed.quote: les groupoïdes S_AΠM_G dépend fonctoriellement du MD-graphe G, pour les morphismes de généralisation
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This suggests a 'modular operad in groupoids', with Dehn-twist extensions, encoding the Teichmüller tower. Approaches to GT-actions via operads of groupoids (e.g. Fresse's work for genus 0) and modular-operad versions are close relatives.

deep.surprise_reason: The geometric content (Dehn-twist extensions at boundary strata, functoriality in contractions) is known in Teichmüller/GT circles. What is notable is the early, explicit move to an abstract categorical axiomatisation: a Boolean quotient-poset condition with functorial Z^A-extensions. It foreshadows later modular-operad and exit-path frameworks, but the page is only the start of it.
transcription_corrections: 'qui stabilise G et contient' should read 'qui stabilise C et contient' (the edge subset C, i.e. the quotient G').
The interlinear insertion above 'les' reads 'groupoïdes', not 'graphes': 'le fait que les groupoïdes S_AΠM_G dépend fonctoriellement du MD-graphe G'.

The axiomatisation sentence should read approximately: 'On va axiomatiser un peu. Les MD-graphes et morphismes de généralisation forment une catégorie, (𝒢), où tous les morphismes sont des épimorphismes.' The 'plus' is struck out.

The left-margin note is largely illegible. It appears to say that 𝒢 can be replaced by a variant: 'La catégorie 𝒢 pourra être celle d'un ... de désigner ... (𝒢) ...'. The current reading is unreliable.
